summary: Pinned model state persists after partial downgrade, causing split-route inference and inconsistent outputs
description:
Issue summary:
A customer on Dedicated capacity experienced inconsistent model responses after a partial downgrade was applied to their pinned model. Some requests continued to route to the previously pinned variant while others were served by the downgraded variant, producing divergent outputs during the same time window.

Impact:
- BrightChat AI reports degraded answer consistency for end-users on two production routes (chat and summarization).
- Customer observed mismatched token billing for identical requests routed to different model variants.
- User-facing functionality was intermittently returning lower-quality summaries.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool: dc-brightchat-us-east
- Region: us-east
- Traffic profile: steady 60 RPS with periodic 500 RPS spikes (batching enabled)

Steps to reproduce (as reported):
1) Customer pinned route "chat/v1" to model rw-infer-rlhf-v2-2026-02.
2) Ops initiated a controlled partial downgrade to rw-7b-ql4-v1 for non-critical traffic using a rollout policy (50% weight).
3) During the rollout window, some requests returned outputs consistent with the older pinned variant while other requests reflected the downgraded model behavior for the same session identifiers.

Observed behavior:
- Split-route inference: Session affinity and version pin metadata appear inconsistent between the read path and the routing layer, resulting in traffic for a single session being split across two model variants.
- Pin persistence: A subset of edge proxies continued to attach the older pin header after the downgrade completed, while controller state indicated the new pinned variant.
- Billing mismatch: Token charges for equivalent requests showed different cost buckets on usage reports.

Expected behavior:
- When a route is pinned, either the pin should be preserved across all request paths until explicitly changed, or the rollout should atomically change pin metadata so all in-flight sessions are consistently routed per the configured policy.

Attachments / Logs / Links:
- Sample request IDs: rq_20260310_aa01, rq_20260310_aa42 (attached logs snippets)
- Routing trace: https://grafana.redwood/trace/route-split/879451
- Billing snapshot: https://billing.redwood/reports/brightchat/consistency-2026-03-10

Initial timeline:
- 2026-03-10 09:12 UTC: Customer reports inconsistent outputs via support case.
- 2026-03-10 09:28 UTC: Support reproduces evidence of split routing in regional logs.
- 2026-03-10 10:05 UTC: Escalated to Serving Runtime and Routing SRE.
- 2026-03-10 14:40 UTC: Temporary mitigation applied (manual unpin + coordinated re-pin to the intended variant).
- 2026-03-11 02:00 UTC: Customer confirms improved consistency but requests postmortem for root cause.

Investigation notes:
- Hypothesis A: Partial downgrade triggered a race between the pinned-session read cache (edge proxies) and the controller write that updated the canonical pin, leaving stale pin metadata in some proxies.
- Hypothesis B: During weight-based rollouts, the routing policy incorrectly treated pin metadata as advisory and applied fallback routing that ignored session affinity for specific edge nodes during a heavy batching spike.
- Logs show a cluster of edge proxies (edge-redis-group-12) with last pin-refresh > 15 minutes before controller commit for the route.
- Routing service debug logs indicate a fallback decision path taken for ~4% of requests when GPU queue depth exceeded threshold. Those fallback decisions did not carry forward the pin header, leading to downgrade routing.

Immediate actions taken:
- Engineering removed batching-induced fallback for pinned routes in the staging policy to prevent routing decisions that drop pin headers.
- Ops performed coordinated cache flush on affected edge proxies (edge-redis-group-12).
- Manual unpin + re-pin sequence executed for BrightChat to re-establish canonical state.

Workaround (customer-facing):
- For urgent consistency, BrightChat temporarily unpinned the route and pinned explicitly to the desired variant after caches were flushed.
- For future rollouts, recommend using strict session-affinity rollout mode (0->100 step) instead of weight-based split for pinned routes.

Next steps / follow-ups:
1) Route: Implement pin-aware fallback policy that preserves pin headers across all fallback codepaths (owner: routing team; ETA: 2026-03-18).
2) Fix: Add stronger cache invalidation hooks so controller commits propagate pin changes synchronously to edge proxies for dedicated pools (owner: serving-runtime; ETA: 2026-03-22).
3) Monitoring: Create alert for pin-refresh-lag > 60s for any edge-redis-group (owner: observability; ETA: 2026-03-13).
4) Customer comms: Draft postmortem and remediation timeline for BrightChat (owner: Support; ETA: 2026-03-15).

Requested information from customer:
- Any scheduled maintenance that overlapped the rollout window.
- Confirmation of sessions/clients that saw divergence (session IDs provided).
- A copy of any client-side retries/backoff behavior that might interact with routing (they provided logs; attached).

investigation: Edge proxies sometimes retained stale pin metadata because cache invalidation was deferred when controller commits were retried. Fallback routing path due to queue-pressure drops pin header; combination produced split routing. Patch to fallback path and cache invalidation hooks validated in staging.
resolution: In progress. Temporary mitigation (manual unpin/re-pin and cache flush) restored customer consistency. Routing patch to preserve pin headers in fallback code merged to staging; cache invalidation automation in review. Billing reconciliation ticket opened with Finance.
